bindings.subject: mergeBlockers
bindings.requirement_text: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

bindings.explanation: Binding fix: the review action is bound by its dotted declaration path APP.actions.submit-review (the earlier bracket form matched no source binding). Substance: REQ-6-5 requires that merging finds 'no valid Request changes', and REQ-6-3-4 requires Request changes to block merging for the current compare commit. The app's own review flow records this decision with the displayed status text 'Changes requested', but mergeBlockers only looks for reviews whose status is exactly 'Request changes', so the blocking decision is never seen and the Merge pull request button stays enabled. The fixture isolates that rule: acme-docs r1 branch release is unprotected, so no approval-count or check condition can mask the defect; the fixture PR uses the real seeded topology (onboarding is genuinely ahead of release at c2) and a non-author reviewer with Admin permission who has no prior decision on the PR, so the control in the precondition (no blocker before the review) holds.

bindings.requirement_text: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

bindings.explanation: Binding fix: the removal handler is bound by its dotted declaration path APP.actions.confirm-remove-member instead of the bracket notation, which matched no source binding. Substance: REQ-2-2-4 and REQ-2-2 require that a removal which would leave the organization with no Owner is rejected and keeps all relationships unchanged ('the last Owner must not be removed'). Seeded org1 has exactly one Owner membership, alice-dev (u1), so removing that member must leave memberships, team memberships and repository grants untouched; confirm-remove-member applies the deletion unconditionally and leaves the organization without any Owner. The fixture is valid: u1 is the sole Owner, u2 and others remain ordinary members, and the handler is invoked with the organization route context the People page supplies.

bindings.subject: confirmRemoveMember
bindings.requirement_text: Open the organization's “People” link to read member usernames. Each removable member has a button named “Member menu <username>”; it opens the menuitem “Remove from organization”, followed by the confirmation button “Remove”. Successful removal makes the complete username absent from People immediately and after reload. A non-Owner viewing the same member has no member-menu button and no Remove from organization menuitem, rather than merely a disabled control. Each independent scenario starts with that member present; the non-Owner is an ordinary organization member. On the “People” page, an organization Owner locates a member, clicks “Remove from organization” in that member's action menu, and clicks “Remove” in the confirmation dialog. The system atomically deletes that member's organization-membership relationship, all of the account's memberships in teams of that organization, and all direct grants to that account on repositories of the organization; if the account still obtains repository permission through another organization Owner status or an undeleted team grant, effective permission is recalculated according to the valid permission rules, otherwise access is denied. The system must not delete the personal account, personal repositories, relationships with other organizations, teams themselves, or team grants; the last Owner must not be removed. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

bindings.subject: createPR
bindings.requirement_text: The valid comparison page is directly accessible to the signed-in contributor. Its Create pull request button opens a form with a field labeled Title, an optional Description field, and a single Create pull request submit button; the comparison-page action is no longer a competing active button. Successful submission shows the entered title as the exact PR heading and visible Open status, and the title survives reload. A title containing only spaces is rejected with Title is required and creates no PR. A user with Write, Maintain, or Admin clicks “Create pull request” on a valid comparison-results page, enters a title containing 1–256 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace and an optional description of at most 65536 characters, confirms distinct base/compare branches with differences, and clicks “Create pull request”. The system atomically creates an Open PR, stores a unique repository-scoped number, source/target branches, current compare commit, current base commit, title, description, author, creation time, and activity record, and redirects to the detail page; if there is no difference, the branches are the same, a Draft or Open PR with the same source/target pair already exists, the title is empty or overlong, the user lacks permission, or submission fails, no record is created. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-2 (Compare Branches Before Opening a Pull Request); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
